name: Jokshan
overview: Jokshan is a male figure in the Bible known primarily as a son of Abraham through his wife Keturah, as recorded in Genesis 25:2. Beyond this unique attribute, there is no additional tribal affiliation or other distinguishing notes provided in Scripture.
namesAndTitles: The name Jokshan appears once in Scripture without a given meaning or special title. It is simply presented as a proper name in Genesis 25:2, with no indication that it was given by God.
familyAndRelationships: Jokshan is explicitly identified as a son of Abraham (referred to as Abram in the text) and Keturah. He is also noted as the father of Sheba and Dedan, establishing his role within the genealogical line described in Genesis 25:2-3.
scriptureSignificance: Jokshan's significance lies in his position as a son of Abraham through Keturah, highlighting the continuation of Abraham's lineage beyond Isaac. His descendants, including Sheba and Dedan, contribute to the broader genealogical and tribal records that form part of the biblical narrative of nations and peoples. Thus, Jokshan represents part of God's providential plan in multiplying Abraham's offspring.
